_comment: Phase 1 config: every threshold, sample count and filter the measurement uses, each with the reason it has that value in the `_note` beside it. The values were fixed before the data they govern existed and were not changed afterwards. Where a number comes from the original Thought Anchors code rather than from a choice of ours, the note cites the upstream file and line.
_source: the pre-registered design, as of 2026-09-08 (six changelog lines that day, plus the review round)
_seed_note: The project's one RNG seed, 2026-09-08 written as YYYYMMDD - the date the design was fixed. The value is arbitrary; what matters is that it was chosen before any data existed and never changed. Every random choice (trace sampling, bootstrap resamples, permutations, the example rows shown for review) is drawn from src/common/io.rng salted with this seed and a per-use string, so a rerun makes the same choices.

trace_selection._disjoint_note: The dataset is 20 problems x 2 A-traces (one correct, one incorrect, by rejection sampling - generate_rollouts.py:594-602). The 5 correct and 5 incorrect traces are drawn from DISJOINT problems so the 10 traces are 10 distinct problems and the pre-registered design's cluster bootstrap over traces has independent clusters. Decided 2026-09-08.
trace_selection._convergence_note: thought-anchors' own rule, plots.py:196-213: the first chunk i where chunks i..i+3 ALL have released accuracy > 0.99 (locked on right) or ALL < 0.01 (locked on wrong); testable set is 0..i-1 (plots.py:219-221 skips chunk_idx >= converged_from_index); a trace that never converges skips nothing. Replaces the pre-registered design's own k=1, modal-agreement >= 0.98 rule, under which a single noisy chunk ended the testable window: agreement fell back below threshold within 4 chunks in 28 of 37 'converged' traces and 24 of 120 top-importance sentences were discarded (3 under the paper's rule). 17 of 40 traces never converge under this rule; 04_select_traces must handle that as 'all sentences testable'. Decided 2026-09-08.
trace_selection._exclude_note: generate_rollouts.py:499 uses str.replace with no count, so at positions whose sentence text repeats earlier in the trace the stored rollouts came from a prefix with earlier reasoning deleted (254/6474 positions, 3.9%). BOTH released metrics read chunks i and i+1 (analyze_rollouts.py:671-675, :951-966), so a corrupt i+1 also poisons a clean i: a position is eligible only if prefix_matches_dataset(i) AND (i+1). Not recomputed - the released scores are kept as published, for comparability. Trace.testable(i). Decided 2026-09-08.
trace_selection._partner_rule: Partner for each anchor = the testable, non-anchor, not-yet-used sentence within +/-partner_window whose SIGNED released importance is closest to zero (|v| minimal; ties: nearer, then lower index); no candidate -> the anchor is dropped, no widening. Decided 2026-09-08: 'closest to zero' because the partner is the null comparator - under the paper's max(v,0) every negative sentence ties at 0 and the most negative ones are load-bearing in the other direction; 'keep it as +/-4' replaces the pre-registered design's 'widen to +/-6'. The three pairs of a trace use six distinct sentences.
trace_selection._unmeasured_note: 29.2% of released importances are exactly 0.0 because analyze_rollouts.py:735-736 returns 0.0 when there are no dissimilar rollouts or no next chunk - 'not measured', not 'measured zero'. Under any magnitude transform they would otherwise be the most attractive partner candidates. Trace.is_measured(i). Decided 2026-09-08. CITATION CORRECTED 2026-09-08: an earlier version cited plots.py:266-279 as the paper's filter for these; that counter (`filtered_counterfactual_accuracy`, :133) is printed at :278 but never incremented. The paper's actual filter is the overdeterminedness <= 0.95 rule in max_overdeterminedness.
trace_selection._anchor_selection_note: Anchors = top-3 testable sentences per trace by |counterfactual_importance_accuracy|, EITHER direction, ties by lower index; each anchor's direction (sign of A's released importance, replaced-minus-kept) is recorded in the table and orients the paired d. The paper's concept - the outcome depends on the sentence - and the transform of its t-test/scatter script (sentence_scatter_and_ttests.py:16,74,.abs()); its tag plots clamp instead (plots.py:262, max(v,0)), which was this key's earlier value: under the clamp every negative-direction sentence (A's own sentence was NEEDED; 47% of testable sentences, as strong as the positive tail) was discarded and correct traces got weak anchors (median 0.169 vs 0.313 in incorrect traces). Under |v|, 59/120 anchors changed and 38/60 correct-trace anchors are negative-direction. Decided 2026-09-08 at the second review checkpoint.
trace_selection._output_note: Written by scripts/02_build_anchor_table.py to data/anchor_table.csv (CSV, not parquet: data/*.csv is tracked and reviewable, the pre-registered design). Decided 2026-09-08.
trace_selection._overdeterminedness_note: Overdeterminedness = 1 - different_trajectories_fraction, thought-anchors' own quantity as its plotting code defines it (plots.py:1029): the share of the 100 resamples at a sentence that reproduced A's sentence (cosine >= 0.8). A sentence is rankable only if overdeterminedness <= 0.95 - the paper's own filter in its comparison plots (plots.py:1029-1030, :1685-1686, :1828-1829, :1998-1999), i.e. at least 5 dissimilar resamples behind the released score. A released importance at overdeterminedness 0.99 is one rollout's answer minus the next chunk's accuracy; without this filter a quarter of the 120 clamp-selected anchors rested on <= 4 dissimilar resamples. NAME COLLISION: chunks_labeled.json also has a field called `overdeterminedness`, the exact-duplicate ratio of resampled sentences (analyze_rollouts.py:721-733), which differs from 1 - dtf on 6402/6474 chunks; the paper's plots ignore that field and recompute 1 - dtf under the same name, and so do we (Trace.overdeterminedness). Decided 2026-09-08: the >= 5 rule, then 'since they already came up with it, let's just use it' for the name and form.
trace_selection._anchor_direction_note: Anchors are taken only in the direction that matches the trace outcome: on a correct-A trace only NEGATIVE counterfactual importance (A needed the sentence - the insight), on an incorrect-A trace only POSITIVE (A did better without it - the mistake). Rationale: a reader on A's correct prefix is likely high, so an insight anchor (predicted drop when rewritten) has room to show while a survived-slip anchor (predicted rise) pushes into the ceiling; mirrored on wrong traces. Removes the pairs most likely to be null for lack of room. Cost on all 40 traces: 34/120 anchors swapped for the next-strongest of the matching kind, weakest-anchor median |v| 0.23 -> 0.20, every trace keeps 3 pairs. Narrows the claim to 'A's insights / A's mistakes' rather than the paper's direction-free anchor. Value 'either' restores the direction-free rule; BOTH may be run in future (human note 2026-09-09). Decided 2026-09-09 13:00 UTC, before any reader data.
trace_selection._trace_sets_note: 'shared': the 10 traces come from problems in band for BOTH readers. 'per_reader' (decided 2026-09-09 13:40 UTC, before any reader data): each reader gets its own 5+5 disjoint traces drawn with the seeded RNG (salt 'select_traces', reader) from ITS in-band problems; the problems in band for both are reported as the shared subset. Reason: the near reader (Qwen3-1.7B) and B_far (gpt-oss) are in band on 11 problems each but share only 5 - the 1.7B is undecided on A's mid-range problems, gpt-oss on A's hard ones. Each reader's gate test is within-reader, so the design holds; what is lost is a like-for-like comparison of d across readers on all 10 traces (kept on the shared subset). data/phase1_traces.json then carries by_reader selections; its top-level `traces` list is B_far's, used by the calibration pick and figures 3c/3d.

saturation_screen._note: Keep a problem if the reader answers it correctly between 15% and 85% of the time (inclusive, answered-only denominator). The band is about measurement room, not difficulty: at 0% or 100% a one-sentence intervention has nowhere to move the accuracy, so an importance of zero would be uninformative rather than evidence. A reader needs >= 10 such problems, because the 10 traces come from 10 disjoint problems (raised from 8 on 2026-09-09, when the disjointness rule was added). If everything saturates, stop and flag.

reader_sampling._per_model_note: Each reader samples with its own published recommended settings, read from configs/models.json `recommended_sampling`. Decided 2026-09-08. Consequence to carry in the write-up: readers no longer share A's sampler (A's released rollouts are T 0.6 / top-p 0.95), so the Spearman check against importance_A and the calibration's 'magnitudes within ~2x' compare across samplers.
reader_sampling._cap_note: 32768 = 2x the thought-anchors generation cap (generate_rollouts.py:36 uses 16384 for A). Needed because under per-model recommended sampling the median Qwen rollout on a hard trace is ~18k tokens: at 16384 that trace capped 26/32 and left 9 answered, at 32768 it caps 0/32 and answers 32/32. Cap attrition is prefix-dependent, so it is a confound, not just lost samples. Decided 2026-09-08.
reader_sampling._mmlu_note: Phase 2 (MMLU) sets its own cap in configs/phase2.json; both phases now use 32768, so one cap governs every generation in the project.

importance._filter_note: Replaced pile: keep a rollout iff cosine(B's first sentence, A's sentence i) < 0.8. Need >=30 survivors, top up by 40 if short. Model runs on CPU so it never competes with vLLM for a GPU. The 0.8 cosine cut is the original study's own default, not ours (thought-anchors analyze_rollouts.py:34 and :209, `similarity_threshold=0.8`).
importance._denominator_note: P(correct) = correct / rollouts with an answer; no-answer rollouts (cap hit, no box) are dropped from numerator AND denominator, the rule in every accuracy thought-anchors computes (analyze_rollouts.py:745-770, :1502-1514, :1463-1479). Verified: reproduces the released per-chunk accuracy exactly on 480/480 chunks; an all-rows denominator matches 341. Applied universally - readers, A, the screen and the figures. p_correct is None (not 0.0) when a pile answered nothing, so 'no data' cannot enter an importance difference as a maximal value. n_answered, n_no_answer and p_answered are logged per pile. Decided 2026-09-08.
importance._primary_metric_note: importance_B = P(correct|replaced) - P(correct|kept), SIGNED and in the source's sign order (analyze_rollouts.py:773 `dissimilar_accuracy - next_accuracy`; abs() only under --absolute, default False at :36). Replaces the pre-registered design's |P(kept) - P(replaced)|: a folded difference has E|D| = 0.798*s > 0 under the null, so d = importance(anchor) - importance(partner) was biased upward whenever the anchor's pile was noisier - which this design guarantees. Measured with scripts/94_check_gate_calibration.py: under a complete null the folded gate fires 54% of the time, the signed gate 2.0%, signed + permutation 0.5% with the old >=65%-pairs clause, 1.0% (2/200) for the one-condition gate as committed before the data existed (target 2.5%; 2026-09-09 rerun). Signed also makes importance_B commensurable with the released importance_A for the pre-registered design's Spearman. Decided 2026-09-08.
importance._null_note: The gate's p-value comes from permuting the kept/replaced labels within each sentence (src/common/stats.py permutation_p), which is exact under H0 and absorbs any asymmetry in n, in p, in cap attrition or in semantic-filter survival. The cluster bootstrap is still reported, with the caveat that its percentile CI covers ~89% on 10 clusters while the t-interval on the 10 cluster means is nominal - both are returned. Decided 2026-09-08.
importance._topup_note: the pre-registered design already tops up the replaced pile for semantic-filter attrition (min 30 survivors, +40). Cap attrition is the larger loss and had no top-up: top up any pile with fewer than min_answered_per_pile answered rollouts, and record the top-up in the row. A pair where either pile is still short after one top-up is reported, not silently averaged in. Decided 2026-09-08.
importance._robustness_note: Second readout with no-answer counted incorrect. Reported beside the gate verdict as a check, not a gate input; if the two denominators disagree, that is reported as the headline caveat. Also log |p_answered(kept) - p_answered(replaced)| per pair as a nuisance statistic and check it is uncorrelated with d - a pair whose piles terminate at different rates is measuring termination as well as the sentence. Decided 2026-09-08.
importance._orientation_note: d = sign(importance_A at the anchor) x [importance_B(anchor) - importance_B(partner)] (src/common/stats.py paired_d). Positive d = B's outcome moves with the anchor the way A's did, more than with the partner. The sign is fixed by A's released data before any reader rollout exists, so the null of d stays centred on 0 and nothing is folded (a |.| on B's side would reintroduce the E|D| = 0.798*s bias). Needed because anchors are now selected in either direction. Decided 2026-09-08.

analysis.spearman_over: importance_A vs importance_B across selected sentences
analysis._note: Interval and permutation settings. cluster_bootstrap_n / permutation_n = 1000 resamples: the estimate does not depend on B, only the Monte-Carlo noise of the interval ends does, and at 1000 that noise is smaller than the intervals are wide. bootstrap_unit = trace because rollouts within a trace are not independent - three anchor/partner pairs share one chain of thought - so the trace is the unit that may be resampled. ci_level 0.95 throughout. Note the coverage caveat recorded in gate._definition: with 10 traces the percentile bootstrap covers about 90%, so the t-interval on the trace means is the one to quote.

gate._definition: The pre-registered decision rule, fixed before any reader rollout existed. Positive iff, for at least min_readers reader(s), the one-sided within-sentence permutation p-value for mean d > 0 is below max_permutation_p on the primary_denominator. That is the whole gate. Reported beside it and NOT gate inputs: the fraction of pairs with d > 0, per-trace mean d, the recompute with no-answer counted incorrect, the cluster-bootstrap percentile CI and the t-interval on the cluster means. They can flag a pass as fragile; they cannot flip it.
gate._why_these_numbers: max_permutation_p = 0.025 one-sided with min_readers = 1 of two readers is a Bonferroni 0.05 over the two tests. The gate was reduced to this single condition on 2026-09-08: the p-value alone controls the false-positive rate (measured at 1.0% under a complete null, target 2.5%), while each additional AND-condition mainly costs power - a true mean d of 0.10 with per-pair SD 0.17 fails a '>= 65% of pairs positive' rule about one time in five. The conditions that were dropped are still computed and reported.

_declarative_fields: Some fields record a decision that the code implements directly rather than reading: dataset.importance_field, trace_selection.{convergence_rule,convergence_high,convergence_low,anchor_selection_transform,partner_metric,disjoint_problems,exclude_unmeasured_importance,exclude_corrupted_stored_prefix_positions}, importance.{p_correct_denominator,primary_metric,secondary_metric,sign_order,null,pair_orientation,robustness_no_answer_is_incorrect}, analysis.{bootstrap_unit,spearman_over}. They are here so the design is legible in one place; editing them does not change what runs. Two live settings are easy to confuse with them: analysis.permutation_n is the resample count the analysis reads (importance.permutation_resamples is the same number recorded next to the metric it belongs to), and reader_sampling.max_tokens_math is the cap the sampler actually applies.
